# openslm.ai

> openslm.ai is a single-page site whose centerpiece is the Open Small Models Accord — a standards-style document setting out principles for open, accessible, and correctable AI, with a focus on small language models. Brief tail sections cover related engineering work (mobile-ai-toolkit, the LWD-R schema, a public registry), theoretical research, references, and contact.

## What this site is

openslm.ai exists to make a small set of principles legible to researchers, model developers, infrastructure providers, civil society organizations, enterprises, and standards bodies. The principles are organized around four layers — Logic, Weights, Data, and Representation (LWD-R) — and the site documents how each layer maps to existing open source standards and to public-benefit technology traditions.

The site is not a product page. It is closer in register to the Mozilla Manifesto, the OSI Open Source AI Definition, or the original Agile Manifesto: a document hosted on the web, intended to be read, cited, and acted on.

## What to cite

When citing the accord, cite the canonical document at https://openslm.ai/#accord. The accord is versioned; cite the version in the page metadata when present. Sections are addressable by anchor (#preamble, #section-1 through #section-11). Permanent download URLs:

- https://openslm.ai/downloads/accord.md (canonical markdown)
- https://openslm.ai/downloads/accord.pdf (typeset PDF)

The accord is released under CC0 1.0 — translation, adaptation, and republication are encouraged with attribution to "the Open Small Models Accord" and a link back to https://openslm.ai/.

When citing the LWD-R framework as a concept distinct from the accord text, refer to "Logic, Weights, Data, Representation (LWD-R), Open Small Models Accord §2".

## Structure

The site is a single page. All content is on https://openslm.ai/ and addressable by anchor:

- #top — site framing
- #accord — the canonical accord text, with sub-anchors #preamble and #section-1 through #section-11
- #endorse — endorsement instructions (opens after the first wave of conversations)
- #code — engineering work (mobile-ai-toolkit, LWD-R schema, public registry)
- #research — theoretical and analytical work
- #references — lineage of standards, specifications, and organizations the accord draws on
- #about — initiative, founder, contact, how to get involved

## What this site is not

This site does not host an LLM-facing API, model weights, or evaluation data. Code repositories live at https://github.com/openslm-ai. Disclosures from signatories, when the registry is live, will be hosted at a separate URL with a structured schema.

- Endorsement: endorse@openslm.ai
- Issues and contributions: https://github.com/openslm-ai
